name: org.machanism.machai:gw-maven-plugin
description: GW Maven Plugin is a Java Maven plugin that integrates Maven builds with Machai Ghostwriter for AI-assisted guided file processing and act execution. It provides project-wide and per-module Maven goals for scanning source, test, documentation, site, configuration, and other project files for embedded guidance, or applying a named act or prompt. The adapter resolves Maven project, module, reactor, settings, classpath, and concurrency context; configures provider/model settings; supports selection and exclusion of paths; and can obtain credentials from Maven settings. Java functional tools discover classes by simple-name regular expression and return reflective structure and source, classpath, and Maven artifact origin metadata. Typical uses include maintaining API documentation, analyzing project structure, performing repeatable guided changes, and automating AI processing inside Maven workflows.

usageContext: Maven builds and Maven plugin execution
Guided file processing using embedded guidance comments
Named act or prompt-driven project transformations
Multi-module Maven projects and reactor builds
Java class discovery and reflective API inspection

constructors.description: Creates class-discovery functional tools and registers the supplied Maven project for subsequent searches and reflective class inspections.

examples.description: Initialize the class tooling from the active Maven project. The helper represents the Maven project context available to a plugin integration; the registered project base directory is used to identify the project during tool calls.

constructors.description: Creates a holder for class discovery and lookup data for one Maven project. The holder builds a project-aware URLClassLoader using the compile classpath and main and test output directories, and records class locations and dependency artifact coordinates for eligible classes.

examples.description: Construct project class metadata from the current MavenProject and load a known class by its fully qualified name.

features.name: gw:gw
features.description: Executes the aggregator guidance workflow using Ghostwriter. The goal configures Maven and provider context, scans selected project files for embedded guidance, and can coordinate multi-module and parallel processing.

examples.description: Step 1: add the plugin to your Maven build and configure the provider model. Step 2: configure credentials in settings.xml under the selected server id. Step 3: place guidance comments in files and run the goal with a focused project path, excluding generated output. Review the resulting changes and run the project tests.

features.name: gw:act
features.description: Executes a named Ghostwriter act or direct prompt against selected project content. It supports instructions, path selection, exclusions, Maven settings credentials, and aggregator processing of modules with submodules handled before parent modules.

examples.snippet:
mvn org.machanism.machai:gw-maven-plugin:1.4.3:act -Dgw.act=review -Dgenai.serverId=my-ai-provider
mvn gw:act -Dgw.act=">Update public API documentation" -Dgw.path=src/main/java
examples.description: Install or declare the plugin in the Maven build, configure provider credentials in settings.xml, then run a named act or provide a prompt-only act prefixed with >. Restrict the scan to the Java source path and review generated documentation changes.

features.name: gw:gw-per-module
features.description: Runs guidance processing in Maven's per-module reactor execution model so each module is processed separately and Maven retains responsibility for module scheduling.

examples.description: Configure the plugin and provider in the build as for the aggregator guidance goal, then invoke this goal in the reactor to process each module independently.

features.name: gw:act-per-module
features.description: Runs act processing once for each Maven reactor module. It works within module boundaries and relies on Maven's reactor scheduling; interactive processor mode is disabled when Maven concurrency exceeds one.

examples.description: After installing/configuring the plugin and provider, run the named act per module and inspect the changes in each module. Supply gw.act explicitly for unattended parallel builds.

features.name: find_class
features.description: Finds fully qualified class names whose simple names completely match the supplied Java regular expression. The scan uses classes visible through the registered Maven project's compile classpath, test output, and main output. Searches producing more than ten matches are rejected so the pattern can be narrowed.

examples.description: Search a registered project's simple class names for Service suffix matches. The returned fully qualified names can be passed to getClassInfo for detailed inspection.

features.name: get_class_info
features.signature: public java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object> org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools.getClassInfo(java.lang.String className, java.io.File projectDir) throws java.lang.ClassNotFoundException
features.description: Loads a fully qualified class through the registered project's class loader and returns reflective metadata including modifiers, direct superclass and interfaces, declared non-private fields and methods, constructors, annotations, classpath path, dependency coordinates, and source path when available.

examples.snippet:
java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object> info = tools.getClassInfo("com.example.orders.OrderService", project.getBasedir());
java.lang.Object declaredMethods = info.get("methods");
examples.description: Inspect a known or previously discovered fully qualified class and use the returned methods, fields, annotations, and origin information to understand or document its API.

features.name: scanProjectClasses
features.description: Registers class metadata for the supplied Maven project. The holder and resulting classpath scan are cached for the project; register again after relevant source, dependency, or build-output changes to refresh the metadata.

examples.description: Register or refresh the active Maven project and search its cached classpath for a controller class by its exact simple name.

features.name: loadClass
features.description: Loads a class using the holder's project-aware class loader. The class name must be fully qualified; ClassNotFoundException is raised when it is unavailable to the loader.

examples.description: Load a project or dependency class by fully qualified name after creating a holder for the Maven project.

features.name: getArtifactId
features.description: Returns Maven dependency coordinates in groupId:artifactId:version form for a class when it originates from a dependency, or null when it is not associated with a dependency artifact.

examples.description: Look up the dependency artifact coordinates associated with a fully qualified class after holder discovery has recorded its origin. The result may be null for project output classes or unknown origins.

examples.title: Install, configure, and run guidance processing
steps: Add org.machanism.machai:gw-maven-plugin:1.4.3 to the build plugins section of pom.xml, or invoke the plugin by its fully qualified Maven coordinates.
Configure the provider/model through the plugin configuration or effective Ghostwriter properties. Add a Maven settings.xml server with credentials and reference it using genai.serverId.
Add guidance comments to project files and choose a focused path and exclusions to avoid generated content.
Run the Maven goal, review the file changes, and execute the project's normal tests.
examples.configuration: Configure model and serverId in the plugin configuration; store the server username and password in Maven settings.xml rather than committing secrets.

examples.title: Run a focused documentation act
steps: Install or declare the Maven plugin and configure a usable Ghostwriter provider and credentials.
Choose a predefined act definition, or provide direct prompt text prefixed with > so it is recognized as a prompt rather than an act name.
Restrict the scan to source or documentation files using gw.path and optionally configure gw.acts for local act definitions.
Run the command and review generated changes before committing them.

examples.title: Discover and inspect a project class
steps: Build the Maven project so main and test output classes are available.
Create ClassFunctionalTools with the active org.apache.maven.project.MavenProject to register its classpath context.
Search simple class names with a Java regular expression; refine the pattern if more than ten matches are returned.
Pass a returned fully qualified class name and the project base directory to getClassInfo to inspect members and origin metadata.
